newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Telefonica profit strong after privatisation.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Telefonica profit strong after privatisation.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica de Espana reported a 15.7 percent jump in first-quarter profits on Monday, just weeks after privatisation and news of a key alliance with British Telecommunications and U.S.-based MCI.
The telecommunications giant said its group attributable profit rose 15.7 percent to 27.87 billion pesetas ($195.2 million) in the first quarter, less than an expected rise of some 20 percent.
But the equity market, convinced of the group's solid medium-term earnings prospects, shrugged aside the more modest rise.

"The immediate response after the announcement of results was negative, but money came right back in because the bourse is strong and an investment in Telefonica continues to be positive medium-term," a broker said.
Shares in Telefonica -- fresh from the extremely successful sale of the state's final 20.9 percent holding earlier this year and flush with its new global alliance -- outpaced the market.
At 1430 GMT, Telefonica was up 120 pesetas, or 3.07 percent, at 4,030, a record. The IBEX index of 35 leading shares was up 2.05 percent at 6,254.42.

"The (earnings) rise was supported by a positive development in the consumption of basic telephone services as well as an expansion in mobile phones and the continuing development of international business," the group said in a statement.
Revenues from abroad reached 108.46 billion pesetas, a rise of 46.7 percent.

Telefonica International -- considered the jewel that attracted international heavyweights BT and MCI to a Telefonica tie-up -- contributed 17.3 percent to the group's total revenue, a rise of three percentage points in a year.
"International business continues to grow strongly, in its size as well as in its contribution to total group results," Telefonica said.

Mobile telephone business also continued to surge. The number of clients in Telefonica's mobile telephone sector rose to 2.55 million, up 110.8 percent over the year-earlier period. Revenues rose to 82.82 billion from 49.06 billion.
Basic telephone services also grew, as Spanish speaking markets expanded.
"The total number of lines in service in Spain and abroad rose 9.5 percent to reach a total of 26.85 million lines at the end of the first quarter," Telefonica said.
The group also managed to lower the costs of its debt financing by 7.7 percent, although this stemmed largely from a sharp decline in Spanish interest rates. ($ = 142.7 Spanish Pesetas)
